title: Engineering Mechanics: Numerical Practice Set 1
instructions: All 40 questions are numerical. Keep rough paper ready; no calculator is allowed in the real exam.
Take g = 10 m/s² wherever the question says so.

questions.question: Two forces of 30 N and 40 N act at a point at right angles to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is:
Two forces of 20 N each act at a point with an angle of 120° between them. The magnitude of their resultant is:
Forces of 10 N and 20 N act at a point with an angle of 60° between them. The magnitude of their resultant is approximately:
The maximum and minimum resultants of two forces are 14 N and 2 N. If the two forces act at right angles, their resultant is:
questions.explanation: P + Q = 14 and P − Q = 2, so P = 8 N and Q = 6 N. At right angles, R = √(8² + 6²) = 10 N.

questions.question: A weight of 100 N hangs from two strings, each making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The tension in each string is:
questions.explanation: Vertical equilibrium: 2T sin 30° = 100, so T = 100 / (2 × 0.5) = 100 N.

questions.question: A force of 100 N is applied at the free end of a 2 m long lever, at an angle of 30° to the lever. The moment of the force about the pivot is:
Two equal and opposite parallel forces of 25 N act 0.2 m apart. The moment of the couple is:
questions.explanation: Moment of a couple = force × arm = 25 × 0.2 = 5 N·m.

questions.question: A simply supported beam AB of span 6 m carries a point load of 12 kN at 2 m from support A. The reaction at support B is:
questions.explanation: Taking moments about A: R_B × 6 = 12 × 2, so R_B = 4 kN (and R_A = 8 kN).

questions.question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 5 kN/m over its whole span. The reaction at each support is:
questions.explanation: Total load = 5 × 4 = 20 kN, shared equally by symmetry: 10 kN at each support.

questions.question: In a lifting machine, an effort of 100 N lifts a load of 600 N. If the velocity ratio is 8, the efficiency of the machine is:
A block weighing 200 N rests on a rough horizontal surface with a coefficient of static friction of 0.3. The minimum horizontal force needed to just move the block is:
The coefficient of friction between a block and an inclined plane is 1/√3. The angle of repose is:

A block of mass 10 kg rests on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.2. Taking g = 10 m/s², the force parallel to the plane needed to just move the block up the plane is approximately:
A body weighing 500 N lies on a rough horizontal surface (μ = 0.25). It is pulled by a force P inclined at 30° above the horizontal. The value of P that just moves the body is approximately:
The height of a triangular lamina is 9 cm. The distance of its centroid from the base is:
questions.explanation: The centroid of a triangle is at h/3 from the base: 9/3 = 3 cm.

questions.question: The centroid of a semicircular lamina of radius 30 mm lies on its axis of symmetry at a distance from the diameter of approximately:
A rectangular section is 6 cm wide and 10 cm deep. Its moment of inertia about the centroidal axis parallel to the width is:
A rectangular section is 6 cm wide and 10 cm deep. Its moment of inertia about its base (the 6 cm side) is:
questions.explanation: By the parallel axis theorem, I = bd³/12 + A(d/2)² = 500 + 60 × 25 = 2000 cm⁴ (= bd³/3).

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a circular section of diameter 20 mm about its diameter is approximately:
The polar moment of inertia of a solid circular section of diameter 20 mm is approximately:
questions.explanation: J = πd⁴/32 = π × 20⁴ / 32 ≈ 15708 mm⁴, twice the moment of inertia about a diameter.

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 20 m/s in 10 s. The distance covered in this time is:
A train moving at 72 km/h is brought to rest with uniform retardation over a distance of 200 m. The retardation is:
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. v² = u² − 2as gives a = 20² / (2 × 200) = 1 m/s².

questions.question: A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance it travels during the 5th second is:
questions.explanation: Distance in the nth second = u + (a/2)(2n − 1) = 0 + 2 × 9 = 18 m.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height it reaches is:
A stone is dropped from the top of a tower 45 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s², the time it takes to reach the ground is:
A projectile is fired at 20 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its horizontal range is approximately:
A projectile is fired at 40 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height it reaches is:
A projectile is fired at 30 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its time of flight is:
A wheel rotates at 600 rpm. Its angular velocity is approximately:
A flywheel starts from rest and reaches an angular velocity of 20 rad/s in 5 s with uniform angular acceleration. The angle it turns through in this time is:
questions.explanation: α = 20/5 = 4 rad/s². θ = ½αt² = ½ × 4 × 25 = 50 rad.

questions.question: A man of mass 60 kg stands in a lift that accelerates upwards at 2 m/s². Taking g = 10 m/s², the force he exerts on the floor of the lift is:
Two masses of 3 kg and 2 kg are connected by a light string passing over a smooth, light pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s², the tension in the string is:
questions.explanation: T = 2m₁m₂g / (m₁ + m₂) = 2 × 3 × 2 × 10 / 5 = 24 N. (The acceleration is 2 m/s².)

questions.question: A car of mass 1000 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest over 50 m by a constant braking force. The braking force is:
questions.explanation: Work done by the brakes = loss of kinetic energy: F × 50 = ½ × 1000 × 20², so F = 4000 N.

questions.question: A pump lifts 100 kg of water through a height of 12 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the power delivered to the water is:
A body of mass 2 kg moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 4 kg and they move together after the collision. Their common velocity is:
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 × 6 = (2 + 4)v, so v = 2 m/s.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.15 kg moving at 20 m/s is hit straight back along its path at 20 m/s. The magnitude of the impulse on the ball is:
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v − u) = 0.15 × (20 − (−20)) = 6 N·s.

questions.question: A ball dropped from a height of 16 m onto a fixed floor rebounds to a height of 4 m. The coefficient of restitution is:
A car of mass 1000 kg travels round a level curve of radius 50 m at 10 m/s. The centripetal force needed is:
A flywheel has a mass moment of inertia of 5 kg·m². The torque needed to give it an angular acceleration of 4 rad/s² is:
A gun of mass 5 kg fires a bullet of mass 0.05 kg at 400 m/s. The recoil velocity of the gun is:
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 5 × V = 0.05 × 400, so V = 4 m/s (backwards).
